question: In 2012 a US business channel aired this: more Americans on welfare than in full-time jobs. Where's the trick?
answer: Twice over. The axis starts at 94 million, so a 7% gap looks like double. And the welfare bar counted everyone in a home where anyone got any means-tested help, Medicaid and school lunches included, babies too, against full-time workers only. Widen what a word covers and the same country tells another story.
move: When a number shocks, ask exactly who it counts and who it leaves out.
ask: When a figure makes me angry, have I checked what its words actually cover?

scene.headline: Welfare vs. full-time jobs
scene.honest: Only 7% apart, and counting different things
scene.label: Americans, millions
scene.found: Yes: the axis starts at 94 million, not at zero.
scene.miss: That part is fair. Look at where the bars begin.

misses.label: Sharp: these count different people. But the bars lie as well.
misses.marks: The numbers are right. It's the heights that shout.

scene.name: Cut axis, wide word
scene.lesson: Bars must start at zero, and labels need reading: here a 7% gap was drawn as double.

source: Media Matters, 2012; US Census Bureau SIPP
reference: Media Matters for America, on Fox Business's 'Welfare vs. Full Time Jobs' graphic, 2012; US Census Bureau, Survey of Income and Program Participation, people in households receiving means-tested benefits, 2011
